Puppeteer (elder guardian): Call tops the guardians within puppeteerElderCallRadius up to this many.
Puppeteer (elder guardian): how far Call counts guardians, and looks for water to raise them from.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerDolphinS: Puppeteer (dolphin): extra swim speed (2.0 = triple). Dolphins breathe air: underwater your air lasts 16x longer (a real dolphin's 4 minutes) but you DO have to surface.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerDolphinL: Puppeteer (dolphin): out of water you flop about and are this much slower (0.7 = 70% slower).
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerDolphinM: Puppeteer (dolphin): ticks out of water (rain counts as water) before you start drying out (vanilla 2400).
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerDolphinI: Puppeteer (dolphin): Inspire cooldown. Right-click: every player and water creature near you gets Dolphin's Grace (much faster swimming).
Puppeteer (dolphin): how long Inspire's Dolphin's Grace lasts.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerDolphinF: Puppeteer (dolphin): health a fish heals (swim into a dropped raw cod / salmon / ..., or someone feeds you one by right-clicking you with it — what a real dolphin eats).
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerAxolotlS: Puppeteer (axolotl): extra swim speed. Endless air underwater; walks fine on land.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerAxolotlM: Puppeteer (axolotl): ticks out of water (rain counts) before you start drying out (vanilla 6000).
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerAxolotlP: Puppeteer Axolotl Play Dead Cooldown Ticks
Puppeteer (axolotl): HOLD right-click to play dead for as long as you like — you lie still, regenerate fast, and every mob after you loses interest. This cooldown starts when you get back up.
Puppeteer (axolotl): health regenerated per second while playing dead.
Puppeteer (axolotl): mobs within this range that are after you lose interest when you play dead.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerPhantomF: Puppeteer (phantom): flight speed (double-tap jump, like the bat; vanilla creative is 0.05). No sprint-flying — unless you have the Flight blessing, which unlocks a fast sprint glide (puppeteerPhantomFlySprintSpeed), exactly as it does for the bat disguise. Burns in daylight.
Puppeteer (phantom): sprint-fly speed with the Flight blessing.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerPhantomB: Puppeteer (phantom): Bite damage — your normal left-click attack (vanilla phantom: 6).

witchmod.configuration.puppeteerPiglinCo: Puppeteer (zombified piglin): right-click a PIG to Convert it — and every pig within this many blocks of it — into zombified piglins.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerBabyZomb: Puppeteer: a BABY zombie-family puppet is this much faster, like a real baby zombie (0.5 = +50%, vanilla's own boost). Every baby puppet is also half size, so you fit where it fits.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerFishSwim: Puppeteer (fish): extra swim speed in water (1.5 = +150%). Underwater you never run out of air.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerFishLand: Puppeteer (fish): out of water you can barely move (0.85 = 85% slower) and you flop about like a real fish (the bounce is the fishFlopPower synergy knob). Your air runs out on land, then you dry out.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerFishLeap: Puppeteer (fish): out of water, Leap launches you this hard along where you're looking (horizontal)...
Puppeteer (fish): ...and this hard upwards, for a big arc. Fish puppets take no fall damage.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerFishDash: Puppeteer (fish): in water, Leap is a quick dash this strong, straight where you're looking.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerFishAtta: Puppeteer (fish): damage of each hit — it's a fish.
witchmod.configuration.puppeteerPufferfi: Puppeteer (pufferfish): hits poison the victim for this long, like a real pufferfish's spines.
Pickpocket: how close you must be to a player to lift from them (blocks). Very close — you're brushing right up against them.
witchmod.configuration.pickpocketCheckIn: Pickpocket: ticks between lift attempts. 100 = every 5s.
witchmod.configuration.pickpocketBaseCha: Pickpocket: chance (0..1) per attempt to lift an item while facing/beside a player.
witchmod.configuration.pickpocketBehindM: Pickpocket: the base chance is multiplied by this when you're BEHIND the victim — sneaking up from behind is far more effective.
witchmod.configuration.pickpocketHotbarW: Pickpocket: relative weight of hotbar slots when choosing what to steal (main-inventory slots are weight 1.0). Low, so you mostly lift from their backpack, not what they're holding.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanRadius.too: Hype Man: how close a player must be to be dragged in as a hype-man and to hear the praise (blocks). Also the pool the random 'speaker' of each line is picked from.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanCooldownTi: Hype Man: minimum ticks between any two praises, across ALL trigger types, so a fight or a pickup spree doesn't turn into a wall of text. 160 = ~8s.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanChance.too: Hype Man: chance (0..1) that an eligible action actually earns praise once the cooldown is up. Below 1 so it stays a treat rather than clockwork.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanAmbientInt: Hype Man: ticks between checks for unprompted 'just being here' praise (still gated by the cooldown and chance above). 120 = every 6s.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanDowntimeIn: Hype Man: ticks between checks for a rarer 'downtime' line — random crowd chatter after a lull with no praise. 600 = every 30s.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanDowntimeTh: Hype Man: how long there must have been NO praise before a downtime line can fire. 400 = 20s.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanBuffChance: Hype Man: chance that a compliment also hands you a random positive potion effect. 0.35 = 35%.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanBuffMinSec: Hype Man: shortest duration of a compliment buff.
witchmod.configuration.hypemanBuffMaxSec: Hype Man: longest duration of a compliment buff.
Tax Man blessing: he'll only turn up to pay you back when no hostile mob is within this radius (blocks) — he waits for it to be safe.
witchmod.configuration.taxmanIdleTicks.t: Tax Man blessing: ticks of you standing roughly still before he'll approach. 60 = 3s.
witchmod.configuration.taxmanGiftEmerald: Tax Man blessing: when the tax bank is EMPTY he brings a gift instead. Emeralds: 1..MAX, uniform.
witchmod.configuration.taxmanGiftGoldMax: Tax Man blessing gift: gold ingots 1..MAX, uniform.
witchmod.configuration.taxmanGiftDiamond: Tax Man blessing gift: diamonds 0..MAX, BIASED toward 0 (min of two rolls), so a fistful of diamonds is a rare treat.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardHealth.t: Bodyguard: the skeleton's max health. Tough — it's meant to soak a beating.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardDamage.t: Bodyguard: melee damage it deals once it's actually ATTACKING an aggressor.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardArmor.to: Bodyguard: armour attribute (on top of any worn armour) — the 'armoured' in the brief.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardSpeed.to: Bodyguard: movement speed. A touch quicker than a player so it can keep up and cut people off.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardFollowDi: Bodyguard: how far from the anchor it's happy to sit before trailing back to them (blocks).
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardTeleport: Bodyguard: if it strays (or the anchor pearls/flies) beyond this, it blinks back to the anchor's side like a tamed wolf (blocks).
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardWarningR: Bodyguard: an intruder this close to the anchor gets WARNED to back off (blocks).
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardAggressi: Bodyguard: an intruder this close, ignoring the warnings, earns AGGRESSION — shoves and warning hits (blocks).
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardLeashRan: Bodyguard: while ATTACKING, it gives up and returns once the aggressor is this far from the anchor (blocks) — it guards a place, it doesn't chase to the ends of the earth.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardThreatLe: Bodyguard: the longer leash used for a genuine ATTACKER (anything that struck you or it), so it actually commits to a real threat instead of standing down the moment they back off.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardWarningH: Bodyguard: damage of a non-committal 'warning hit' during AGGRESSION. Low — it's a shove, not an execution.
Bodyguard: minimum ticks between warning hits.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardPatience: Bodyguard: ticks an intruder can keep crowding at AGGRESSION range before the bodyguard loses patience, draws its sword and actually attacks them (no attack from them needed). 100 = 5s. This is what makes it engage instead of shoving forever.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardWarnings: Bodyguard: how many spoken warnings it must actually deliver to a lingering intruder before patience is allowed to draw steel — so it never silently jumps to violence. (Being physically attacked still triggers immediate self-defence, warnings or not.)
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardChatRadi: Bodyguard: only players within this radius hear it speak (blocks) — its lines are local, not server-wide.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardRespawnT: Bodyguard: after it dies, the blessing is NOT lost — a replacement is hired this many ticks later. 7200 = 6 minutes.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardDialogue: Bodyguard: minimum ticks between one spoken dialogue tree and the next during a confrontation (idle 'ambient' chatter is 3x rarer). 100 = ~5s — chatty enough to feel alive without talking over itself.
Bodyguard: ticks between successive lines WITHIN one dialogue tree.
witchmod.configuration.bodyguardStruggle: Bodyguard: how many blink-back teleports within the struggle window (usually because you're airborne and it can't keep up) before it grumbles a 'struggle' line.
Bodyguard: the rolling window for counting struggle teleports. 80 = 4s.
Bodyguard: minimum ticks between two struggle grumbles, so a long flight doesn't spam chat.
witchmod.configuration.guardedAllyStrong: Guarded Ally (Guardian Angel + Bodyguard): duration of the FULL frenzy the angel whips the bodyguard into when you're attacked (Strength/Speed/Resistance). 12 = 12s.
Guarded Ally: amplifier of the strong frenzy's buffs (0 = level I, 1 = level II, ...).
witchmod.configuration.guardedAllySoftSe: Guarded Ally: duration of the SOFTER frenzy left in the bodyguard when the angel dies. 8 = 8s.
witchmod.configuration.guardedAllySoftAm: Guarded Ally: amplifier of the soft frenzy's buffs (0 = level I).
witchmod.configuration.guardedAllyCooldo: Guarded Ally: minimum ticks between one under-attack frenzy trigger and the next, so a run of hits doesn't re-buff every tick. 100 = 5s.
witchmod.configuration.angelsGrudgeIrrit: Angel's Grudge (Guardian Angel + Solicitor): the low end of the hidden irritation timer that must fill (while the trader is around) before the angel hunts it down. 1800 = 90s.
Angel's Grudge: the high end of the hidden irritation timer (a bit of randomness on top). 3600 = 3min.
witchmod.configuration.angelsGrudgeCoold: Angel's Grudge: how long the solicitor is forced to lie low after the angel kills its trader. 6000 = 5 minutes.
witchmod.configuration.soulBondRadius.to: Soul Bond: how close the nearest living thing must be to become your bound (blocks). The bond continuously re-picks the nearest, so in a 1v1 it latches onto your opponent and with a pet at your heels it latches onto the pet — which is the whole deterrent.
witchmod.configuration.soulBondDamageSha: Soul Bond: fraction of the damage YOU take that your bound takes instead. 0.4 = they eat 40%, you eat the remaining 60%. Their share bypasses armour (it's a soul tether).
witchmod.configuration.soulBondRebindInt: Soul Bond: ticks between re-picking the nearest living thing to bind. 20 = once a second.
witchmod.configuration.soulBondParticleI: Soul Bond: ticks between the constant golden particles emitted on the bound entity.
witchmod.configuration.fullnessDrainRate: Fullness: fraction of the NORMAL hunger drain that actually sticks. 0.2 = hunger (and its hidden saturation) deplete at a fifth of the usual rate, so you rarely need to eat.
witchmod.configuration.armyRadius.toolti: Army: radius (blocks) within which hostile mobs go neutral toward you and rally to your defence when something hits you.
witchmod.configuration.armyDefendDuratio: Army: ticks the nearby horde keeps swarming whatever last hit you. 600 = 30s.
witchmod.configuration.armyCheckInterval: Army: ticks between sweeps that keep hostiles off you (and re-aim the swarm). Low, so mobs barely get a swing in before being pacified.
witchmod.configuration.armySameTypeExclu: Army: if true, the swarm won't turn on its OWN kind — a zombie that hit you won't be attacked by other zombies, but skeletons etc. still will.
witchmod.configuration.reflectVelocityMu: Reflect: speed multiplier on a projectile sent back at its shooter. 1.5 = it returns half again as fast as it arrived — harder to dodge, but dodgeable (it doesn't home).
witchmod.configuration.reflectInaccuracy: Reflect: spread on the return shot. 0.0 = dead-precise at the attacker; raise for sloppier aim (vanilla arrows use ~1.0).
witchmod.configuration.reflectGladiatorV: Reflect+Gladiator synergy: extra speed multiplier on a reflected shot, so it flies further before dropping.
witchmod.configuration.peaceSpawnRateMul: Peace: fraction of hostile NATURAL spawns near you that are still ALLOWED. 0.3 = ~70% of them are quietly cancelled, so far fewer monsters appear around you.
witchmod.configuration.peaceRadius.toolt: Peace: radius (blocks) around you that spawn suppression and detection reduction apply.
witchmod.configuration.peaceDetectionMul: Peace: fraction of a hostile's NORMAL follow range at which it can still notice you. 0.4 = mobs only lock onto you at 40% of the usual distance — the opposite of Popularity.
witchmod.configuration.peaceCheckInterva: Peace: ticks between sweeps that strip too-distant aggro and check for the discovery moment.
witchmod.configuration.luckAttributeBonu: Luck: how much is added to your vanilla LUCK attribute. Nudges loot-table rolls (fishing, chests) toward better outcomes. 5.0 is a big, if quiet, boost.
witchmod.configuration.sirenCheckInterva: Siren's Call: ticks between longing updates. 10 = twice a second.
witchmod.configuration.sirenLongingMax.t: Siren's Call: the longing meter's ceiling. Stages are read against this.
witchmod.configuration.sirenDryGain.tool: Siren's Call: longing gained per check while OUT of water. At the default check rate, 0.2 fills an empty meter in roughly four minutes of staying dry.
witchmod.configuration.sirenWaterDrain.t: Siren's Call: longing lost per check while in water, AFTER the grace period. Much faster than it builds — a proper dip settles you quickly.
witchmod.configuration.sirenWaterGraceTi: Siren's Call: minimum ticks you must stay in water before the longing begins to DROP. During this grace the meter holds and the magenta mind-control shader fades out — so by the time it's actually falling, the screen is clear again. 60 = 3s.
witchmod.configuration.sirenStage1Thresh: Siren's Call stage 1 — UNEASE: faint bubbles and a rare water drip, no penalty yet.
witchmod.configuration.sirenStage2Thresh: Siren's Call stage 2 — YEARNING: Mining Fatigue I + the occasional yearning cue.
witchmod.configuration.sirenStage3Thresh: Siren's Call stage 3 — RESTLESSNESS: Mining Fatigue II, a more frequent cue, Nausea flickers.
witchmod.configuration.sirenStage4Thresh: Siren's Call stage 4 — HEAVINESS: Slowness I on land.
witchmod.configuration.sirenStage5Thresh: Siren's Call stage 5 — THE SEA'S GRIP: Slowness II on land + intermittent pull-bursts toward water (the sea testing its hold; still resistible between bursts).
witchmod.configuration.sirenStage6Thresh: Siren's Call stage 6 — THE MARCH: continuous movement hijack to the water, magenta shader.
witchmod.configuration.sirenShaderMaxAlp: Siren's Call: peak opacity of the magenta mind-control overlay, 0..1. A tint, not a wall.
witchmod.configuration.sirenWaterSearchR: Siren's Call: how far to look for water to be dragged toward, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.sirenPullForce.to: Siren's Call: a small server-side velocity tug toward the water on top of the hijacked walk, so even mid-air or on ice you drift the right way.
witchmod.configuration.sirenDrownedSooth: Siren's Call: how close a Drowned must be to soothe you, in blocks. They protect their own — nearby Drowned slow the longing and won't turn on the victim.
witchmod.configuration.sirenDrownedGainM: Siren's Call: longing-gain multiplier while a Drowned is watching over you. Below 1.
witchmod.configuration.basementStartInte: Basement Dweller: ticks between burns WHEN YOU FIRST step into the sun (the slow start).
witchmod.configuration.basementEndInterv: Basement Dweller: ticks between burns once the ramp is fully wound up (the fast end).
witchmod.configuration.basementRampTicks: Basement Dweller: how long (ticks) continuous sun takes to decay from the start interval to the end interval. 500 = 25s.
witchmod.configuration.basementDamage.to: Basement Dweller: damage per burn in direct daylight, in half-hearts.
witchmod.configuration.basementHelmetInt: Basement Dweller: a hat SLOWS the burns rather than softening them — the interval is multiplied by this while your head slot is occupied. Above 1 (2.5 = burns 2.5x further apart), but never infinite: you still cook, just slower.
witchmod.configuration.claustrophobiaSta: Claustrophobia: ticks between bites WHEN YOU FIRST get boxed in (the slow start).
witchmod.configuration.claustrophobiaEnd: Claustrophobia: ticks between bites once the ramp is fully wound up (the fast end).
witchmod.configuration.claustrophobiaRam: Claustrophobia: how long (ticks) staying boxed-in takes to decay from the start interval to the end interval. 200 = 10s.
witchmod.configuration.claustrophobiaDam: Claustrophobia: damage per tick while indoors, in half-hearts. Milder than Basement Dweller's sun by design.
witchmod.configuration.envCombinedGraceT: Basement+Claustrophobia together: extra grace (ticks) after entering a damage condition before ANY damage starts, since suffering both at once is brutal. 70 = 3.5s. Applied only while both curses are active; swaps off the moment one is removed.
witchmod.configuration.envCombinedInterv: Basement+Claustrophobia together: multiply the gap between hits by this while both are on.
witchmod.configuration.envCombinedDecayM: Basement+Claustrophobia together: multiply the ramp/decay time by this while both are on.
witchmod.configuration.stickDriftCameraC: Stick Drift: percent chance the rolled drift is a CAMERA drift rather than a MOVEMENT one. Decided once when the curse lands and fixed thereafter.
witchmod.configuration.stickDriftGapMinT: Stick Drift: shortest calm gap between drift episodes, in ticks.
witchmod.configuration.stickDriftGapMaxT: Stick Drift: longest calm gap between drift episodes, in ticks.
witchmod.configuration.stickDriftDuratio: Stick Drift: intensity × duration is held roughly constant at this many tick-units, so a stronger drift lasts a shorter time and vice versa (the controller-drift joke). Episode length = this ÷ intensity, clamped to the bounds below.
Stick Drift: shortest an episode can last regardless of intensity, in ticks.
Stick Drift: longest an episode can last regardless of intensity, in ticks.
witchmod.configuration.stickDriftMoveSca: Stick Drift: movement drift at full intensity, as a fraction of full stick input.
witchmod.configuration.stickDriftCameraS: Stick Drift: camera drift at full intensity, in degrees per tick.
witchmod.configuration.wonkyDriftStrengt: Wonky: how hard your movement wanders sideways while walking, as a fraction of full strafe. Kept small — it should feel like you can't quite hold a line, not like being shoved.
witchmod.configuration.wonkySprintMultip: Wonky: how much the sideways wander is amplified while sprinting — you commit harder, so the wobble is worse.
Wonky: how many ticks one full left-right wander cycle takes. Longer = a lazier weave that's harder to consciously correct for; shorter = a jitterier stagger.
witchmod.configuration.flatFootedStepDis: Flat Footed: blocks of travel between amplified footfalls. Lower = more frequent stomps.
Flat Footed: volume of the amplified footstep. Vanilla steps are ~0.15, so this is cartoonishly loud — that's the joke, and it's what makes you trackable.
witchmod.configuration.flatFootedSneakVo: Flat Footed: multiplier applied while sneaking. Below 1 so tiptoeing is a bit quieter — but never silent, so sneaking away still gives you away.
witchmod.configuration.flatFootedShakeRa: Flat Footed: how close another player must be to feel the footstep camera-shudder.
witchmod.configuration.flatFootedShakeSt: Flat Footed: peak footstep camera-shudder amplitude in degrees. Slight — a nudge, not the Heavyweight jolt.
witchmod.configuration.flatFootedShakeTi: Flat Footed: how long each footstep shudder lasts, in ticks.
witchmod.configuration.flatFootedDetecti: Flat Footed: extra blocks of FOLLOW_RANGE handed to nearby hostile mobs, so your racket reaches their ears from further off. Slight on purpose.
Flat Footed: how far out hostile mobs get that detection bonus applied, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsCheckI: Broken Bonds: ticks between hate-meter updates on nearby owned pets.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsRadius: Broken Bonds: how close one of your pets must be for its resentment to build, in blocks. Beyond this its meter cools off instead.
Broken Bonds: how much hate a pet must accumulate before it snaps and untames.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsProxim: Broken Bonds: hate per check while a pet is RIGHT next to you (it scales down with distance, so being across the radius barely registers). Deliberately slow.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsFollow: Broken Bonds: extra hate per check while a pet is actively trailing you around (standing, not sitting) — spending time in your company wears on it.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsRideGa: Broken Bonds: extra hate per check while you are RIDING the pet. Being sat on is the fastest way to lose a friend.
Broken Bonds: hate lost per check when a pet is out of range or otherwise not building. Similar to the proximity rate, so leaving it alone genuinely calms it down.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsRandom: Broken Bonds: +/- fraction of jitter on each hate change, so the exact moment a pet snaps is never perfectly predictable. 0.3 = up to 30% either way.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsFleeTi: Broken Bonds: how long a freshly-untamed pet's legs are hijacked to storm off. 200 = 10s.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsFleeDi: Broken Bonds: how far ahead it aims each leg of that escape, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.brokenBondsFleeSp: Broken Bonds: movement speed multiplier while storming off.
witchmod.configuration.oversharerInterva: Oversharer: shortest gap between leaks, in ticks. 1800 = 1.5min.
Oversharer: longest gap between leaks, in ticks. 6000 = 5min.
witchmod.configuration.clumsyBaseChanceP: Clumsy: percent chance the very next block you place goes wrong, from a clean slate.
witchmod.configuration.clumsyPerBlockCha: Clumsy: extra percent added for each block placed without a slip. The chance ramps up the longer you go clean, then resets the moment something goes wrong.
witchmod.configuration.clumsyMaxChancePe: Clumsy: the ceiling that ramp climbs to, in percent.
witchmod.configuration.clumsyOrientalOri: Clumsy: for a block WITH an orientation (stairs, doors, logs...), percent of slips that come out facing the wrong way. This plus the next two should total 100.
witchmod.configuration.clumsyOrientalLoc: Clumsy: for an oriented block, percent of slips that land in the wrong spot.
witchmod.configuration.clumsyPlainLocati: Clumsy: for a plain block with no orientation, percent of slips that land in the wrong spot. This plus the next should total 100.
witchmod.configuration.taxesCheckInterva: Taxes: ticks between checks for whether you've been careless enough to be worth a visit.
witchmod.configuration.taxesScanRadius.t: Taxes: how far the Tax Man reaches for chests, floor items and your person, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.taxesMinValueTrig: Taxes: how much VALUE must be within reach before a visit is worth his time (see taxesItemValues). This is the counterplay made concrete — stay under it and he never comes.
witchmod.configuration.taxesHaulValueCap: Taxes: how much VALUE he takes in one visit before declaring himself satisfied. Weighted rather than counted, so he can't strip a stack of netherite the way he would a stack of copper. Kept low on purpose: this should be an irritation, not a robbery.
witchmod.configuration.taxesDefaultItemV: Taxes: value of anything in the witchmod:valuables tag that isn't listed in taxesItemValues — including modded ores, which is why this exists.
witchmod.configuration.taxesItemValues.t: Taxes: per-item worth, as "item=value". Storage blocks are worth roughly 9x their ingot because that's what they're made of. Anything omitted falls back to taxesDefaultItemValue.
witchmod.configuration.taxesBankCapacity: Taxes: how many stacks the world-wide tax bank can hold. ⚠ THIS IS A MEMORY LIMIT, NOT A BALANCE ONE, AND IT MUST NEVER VOID ITEMS. The bank is a SavedData list that persists forever and is only drained by the Tax Man BLESSING, so without a ceiling it grows without bound for the life of the world. When it is full the correct behaviour is to STOP TAKING — the Taxes curse is refused at the table and by command, and the Tax Man leaves things where they are. Never discard. Sized far larger than one visit's haul so it comfortably holds many taxations.
witchmod.configuration.taxesBankWarnAtPe: Taxes: percentage full at which commands start warning that the bank is filling up.
witchmod.configuration.taxesCooldownTick: Taxes: ticks before he may return after a visit. 6000 = 5min. He does come back — the curse isn't spent by one audit.
witchmod.configuration.taxesCollectInter: Audit: ticks between individual seizures. Item-by-item so you can watch it happen and swear at him, but brisk (7 = ~0.35s) so a full chest doesn't take an age.
Audit: how long he stands there ominously before starting work. 20 = 1s.
witchmod.configuration.taxesLeaveTicks.t: Audit: how long he lingers after finishing before vanishing. 25 = ~1.25s.
witchmod.configuration.taxesGiveUpSweeps: Audit: how many fruitless sweeps before he gives up and leaves.
witchmod.configuration.taxesEnderChestAf: Audit: fruitless sweeps before he places his OWN ender chest to go through yours — the answer to hiding everything in the one container he can't otherwise reach.
witchmod.configuration.taxesChatRadius.t: Taxes: how far away other players can hear him narrating, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefCheckI: Comic Relief: ticks between rolls. 100 = every 5s.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefLowHea: Comic Relief: at or below this health, in half-hearts, the sky starts taking an interest. 6.0 = three hearts.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefStrike: Comic Relief: percent chance per check of a killing bolt while you're low. Small on purpose — the joke only lands if it's genuinely unexpected.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefItemSt: Comic Relief Item Strike Chance Percent
Comic Relief: percent chance per check of a bolt landing on a pile of your dropped items instead, destroying them.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefItemPi: Comic Relief Item Pile Scaling Percent

Comic Relief: extra percent added to the item-strike chance for each item beyond the minimum pile size. A big pile of your worldly goods lying in a field is exactly the shot the joke wants, so the bigger it is the likelier the sky is to take it.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefItemCh: Comic Relief Item Chance Cap Percent
Comic Relief: ceiling for that scaled item-strike chance, per check.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefItemPi: Comic Relief: how many item entities nearby count as a pile worth striking.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefItemSc: Comic Relief: how far to look for that pile, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefPosthu: Comic Relief: percent chance that dying earns you one more bolt on the spot a moment later — which torches the drops you left behind. Deliberately rare, and deliberately kicking you while you're down; that IS the joke.
Comic Relief: ticks after death before that parting bolt lands. Long enough that the death screen is already up, which is what sells it.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefThunde: Comic Relief: all of the above chances are multiplied by this while it's thundering.
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefSmiteB: Comic Relief+Thunder synergy: extra visual bolts rained down in a quick barrage when the killing bolt fires (still kills the same way, just funnier).
witchmod.configuration.comicReliefSmiteS: Comic Relief+Thunder synergy: ticks between the barrage's extra bolts.
witchmod.configuration.thirstMax.tooltip: Thirst Meter: bar size, in points. 20 = ten droplets, matching hunger.
witchmod.configuration.thirstIdleDrainPe: Thirst Meter: thirst-exhaustion added per tick while doing nothing. At the default exhaustion-per-point of 4.0, 0.01 works out to one droplet per 20s of standing still.
witchmod.configuration.thirstWalkDrainPe: Thirst Meter: extra thirst-exhaustion per tick while walking.
witchmod.configuration.thirstSprintDrain: Thirst Meter: extra thirst-exhaustion per tick while sprinting or swimming. This is the point of the curse — it is meant to stop a target being very active.
witchmod.configuration.thirstActionDrain: Thirst Meter: thirst-exhaustion per strenuous action — mining a block, landing a hit.
witchmod.configuration.thirstExhaustionP: Thirst Meter: how much accumulated thirst-exhaustion costs one point off the bar. Mirrors vanilla's hunger model, where 4.0 exhaustion costs a haunch.
witchmod.configuration.thirstDehydration: Thirst Meter: drain multiplier while the Dehydration effect is on you. 4.0 takes the idle rate from one droplet per 20s down to one per 5s — hot biomes apply Dehydration, so this is what sets the pace out in a desert.
witchmod.configuration.thirstSaturationP: Thirst Meter: how much hidden saturation each restored point also grants. Saturation is spent BEFORE the visible bar, exactly like hunger — it's the grace period that stops a freshly-filled bar from starting to tick down the instant you finish drinking.
witchmod.configuration.thirstFullBonusHe: Thirst Full Bonus Heal Interval Ticks
Thirst Meter: ticks between bonus heals while BOTH hunger and thirst are completely full. This is the reward for keeping on top of it, stacked on vanilla's own regen.
Thirst Meter: health restored per bonus heal, in half-hearts.
witchmod.configuration.thirstHotBiomeTem: Thirst Meter: biome base temperature at or above which you count as being somewhere hot and start dehydrating. 1.0 catches desert, badlands, savanna and the Nether; jungle sits just under at 0.95.
witchmod.configuration.thirstActivityDeh: Thirst Meter: how many points of the bar you must burn through while it's already below half before sustained activity brings on Dehydration by itself.
witchmod.configuration.thirstDehydration: Thirst Meter: how long Dehydration lasts once applied, in ticks. Refreshed while you remain in a hot biome.
witchmod.configuration.thirstSprintCutof: Thirst Meter: at or below this many points you can no longer sprint.
witchmod.configuration.thirstEmptyDamage: Thirst Meter: damage per interval at an empty bar. Uses the mod's own dehydration damage type, which is fatal on EVERY difficulty and bypasses armour.
Thirst Meter: ticks between those damage ticks. 40 = 2s.
witchmod.configuration.thirstRestoreWate: Thirst Meter: points restored by a water bottle.
witchmod.configuration.thirstRestorePoti: Thirst Meter: points restored by any other potion.
witchmod.configuration.thirstRestoreRawW: Thirst Meter: points restored by drinking straight from a water source.
witchmod.configuration.thirstRawWaterRis: Thirst Meter: percent chance drinking untreated water makes you ill — weak Poison, or Dehydration, which is the crueller of the two.
witchmod.configuration.thirstRestoreRawF: Thirst Meter: points restored by raw food (uncooked meat and fish).
witchmod.configuration.thirstRestoreNatu: Thirst Meter: points restored by natural food — the water-rich plant stuff (melon, apples, berries, carrots). Uses the same category split as the Allergic curse.
witchmod.configuration.thirstRestoreOthe: Thirst Meter: points restored by anything else edible — cooked meat, bread, stews. The spec only named raw and natural, so this is the judgement call: dry, processed food is worth a little but nothing like fruit. Set to 0 if it should be worth nothing at all.
Pandora's Box: how many random curses it holds on you at once. These are ON TOP of the normal curse limit (they don't count toward it).
witchmod.configuration.pandorasBoxSwapSe: Pandora's Box: seconds between swaps — each swap trades the OLDEST held curse for a new random one.
Shadow: how far behind you (ticks) your shadow retraces your exact path. 42 = 2.1 seconds. Stand still for this long and it reaches you.
witchmod.configuration.shadowMaxChaseTic: Shadow: chases come in bouts. After chasing (risen) for this many ticks it gives up and vanishes, as if you'd gone into water, then returns after shadowRespawnTicks + the delay. 1440 = 1.2 minutes.
witchmod.configuration.shadowSummonTicks: Shadow: length (ticks) of its summoning — it claws up out of the ground and can't catch anyone until it has fully risen.
witchmod.configuration.shadowSpawnMinDis: Shadow: idle protection for SPAWNING only — it won't form while its spawn point (your position shadowDelayTicks ago) is closer to you than this, so standing still can't make it appear on top of you. It waits until you've moved away. Once it exists, the normal chase rules apply.
witchmod.configuration.shadowRespawnTick: Shadow: after it vanishes (you went into water, changed dimension, or it just caught you), how long (ticks) before it starts following again. It then re-forms shadowDelayTicks behind you.
witchmod.configuration.shadowCatchDistan: Shadow: how close (blocks, centre to centre) it has to get to catch — and kill — you.
witchmod.configuration.shadowMusicDistan: Shadow: its chase music (the Snail's) starts when it's within this many blocks of you, and swells to full volume as it closes in. Only the hunted player hears it.
witchmod.configuration.pestsChancePercen: Pests: percent chance per block mined that silverfish come out of it. Mining is a very high-frequency action, so this is much lower than it looks — at 8% a normal tunnelling session still produces a steady trickle.
witchmod.configuration.pestsMobHitChance: Pests: percent chance per melee hit on a mob that silverfish crawl out of it (hitting a silverfish never spawns more).
witchmod.configuration.pestsMaxNearby.to: Pests: skip spawning if this many silverfish are already near the victim. A necessary guard rather than balance — silverfish CALL MORE SILVERFISH out of stone when hit, so without a ceiling a mining session can snowball into an unrecoverable swarm.
witchmod.configuration.pestsNearbyRadius: Pests: radius the nearby-silverfish ceiling is measured over, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.heavyweightBaseBr: Heavyweight: flat ticks added to every break, before hardness is considered. Keeps even the softest block from vanishing the instant you step on it.
witchmod.configuration.heavyweightHardne: Heavyweight: ticks added per point of block hardness. Roughly: leaves 0.8s, dirt 1.1s, stone 2.4s, planks 3.0s, iron block 6.8s, obsidian ~60s. Obsidian stays a real deterrent without being literally impossible, which a higher multiplier made it.
witchmod.configuration.heavyweightWarnFr: Heavyweight: how far through the break the audible creaking starts, 0-1. Before this point the warning is purely visual.
witchmod.configuration.heavyweightCollap: Heavyweight: how far the collapse spreads to neighbouring blocks, in blocks. The floor giving way should take a chunk of itself with it, not punch one neat hole.
Heavyweight: percent chance each neighbouring block in range goes too. Below 100 so the hole is ragged rather than a perfect square.
witchmod.configuration.heavyweightShakeT: Heavyweight: how long the camera rattles after a collapse. 12 = 0.6s.
witchmod.configuration.heavyweightShakeS: Heavyweight: peak camera-shake amplitude in degrees. Decays to nothing over the window.
witchmod.configuration.floorIsLavaGraceT: Floor Is Lava: how long you may stand still before it starts hurting. 100 = 5s — long enough to craft, read a sign or check a chest, short enough that you can never settle.
witchmod.configuration.floorIsLavaDamage: Floor Is Lava Damage Interval Ticks
Floor Is Lava: ticks between burns once the grace period has run out. 20 = 1s.
witchmod.configuration.floorIsLavaBaseDa: Floor Is Lava: damage on the FIRST burn, in half-hearts.
witchmod.configuration.floorIsLavaRampPe: Floor Is Lava Ramp Per Burn
Floor Is Lava: extra damage added per consecutive burn. The ramp is the whole point — standing still has to get worse the longer you do it, or it's just a slow tax.
witchmod.configuration.floorIsLavaMaxDam: Floor Is Lava: the cap the ramp climbs to, in half-hearts per burn. Without a cap an AFK player is simply executed, which isn't a joke, it's a disconnect.
witchmod.configuration.floorIsLavaMoveme: Floor Is Lava Movement Reset Distance

Floor Is Lava: how far you must move to be counted as moving and reset the timer. Small, so shuffling on the spot genuinely counts — but not zero, or camera-only movement and sub-block jitter would keep you safe forever.
witchmod.configuration.outcastRevealDist: Social Outcast: how close someone must get before you can see them at all, in blocks. Small on purpose — they should be able to stand right next to you before appearing.
witchmod.configuration.outcastDamageReve: Social Outcast: how long someone stays visible after hitting you. 400 = 20s. Once it lapses without another hit they vanish again, so a fight keeps them on screen but a single ambush doesn't reveal them permanently.
witchmod.configuration.outcastHidesVilla: Social Outcast: whether villagers are hidden too, or only players.
witchmod.configuration.minorInconvenienc: Minor Inconvenience: shortest gap between window renames. 600 = 30s.
Minor Inconvenience: longest gap between window renames. 2400 = 2min.
witchmod.configuration.screensaverEpisod: Screensaver: shortest bouncing episode, in ticks. 400 = 20s.
Screensaver: longest bouncing episode, in ticks. 900 = 45s.
witchmod.configuration.screensaverDutyPe: Screensaver: roughly what percentage of the time is spent BOUNCING, excluding the transitions in and out. The idle gap is derived from this and the episode length, so changing episode length keeps the same overall rhythm automatically.
witchmod.configuration.screensaverTransi: Screensaver: how long the shrink and grow take, in ticks. 80 = 4s each way. Deliberately slow and eased — a snap resize is jarring and reads as a crash rather than a joke.
witchmod.configuration.screensaverWindow: Screensaver: the shrunk window's size as a percentage of the monitor. Kept LARGE on purpose — a tiny window bouncing fast is a motion-sickness generator, and you still have to be able to play.
witchmod.configuration.screensaverSpeedP: Screensaver: bounce speed in pixels per tick. Low by design, for the same reason.
witchmod.configuration.dwarfismModelScal: Dwarfism: size multiplier. 0.5 is half height — and because vanilla's SCALE attribute drives the bounding box as well as the model, you genuinely fit through 1-block gaps.
witchmod.configuration.dwarfismHealthMul: Dwarfism: max-health multiplier. 0.5 = 10 hearts down to 5.
witchmod.configuration.dwarfismCanRidePl: Dwarfism: whether right-clicking another player lets you ride them.
witchmod.configuration.dwarfismCanRideVi: Dwarfism: whether right-clicking a villager lets you ride them.
witchmod.configuration.neutralAggroRadiu: Neutral Aggression: how close a neutral mob must be before it turns on you, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.neutralAggroCheck: Neutral Aggression: ticks between sweeps for anything neutral nearby.
witchmod.configuration.neutralAggroTurns: Neutral Aggression: whether YOUR OWN tamed animals turn on you too. On by default — your own dog deciding it hates you is the best thing this curse does.
witchmod.configuration.magnetRadius.tool: Magnet: how close a projectile must be before it starts curving toward you, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.magnetSteerStreng: Magnet: how sharply a projectile is bent toward you each tick, 0-1. This steers the DIRECTION only and preserves the projectile's speed — accelerating them instead would make arrows hit harder, which isn't the joke.
Magnet: whether YOUR OWN projectiles curve back at you. Off by design — having your own arrows boomerang is just unplayable rather than funny.
witchmod.configuration.magnetMaxProjecti: Magnet: cap on projectiles steered per tick, so an arrow barrage can't cost the server.
Magnet: a SUBTLE per-tick velocity nudge (blocks/tick) that drifts nearby HARMFUL things (primed TNT) toward you within magnetRadius. Kept small so it's a creeping menace, not a yank. 0 disables the hazard pull.
witchmod.configuration.magnetStormInterv: Magnet+Thunder synergy: ticks between rolls for a real lightning strike drawn onto you during a thunderstorm (only under open sky).
witchmod.configuration.magnetStormChance: Magnet+Thunder synergy: percent chance per roll that lightning strikes you while it's thundering.
witchmod.configuration.heavyFallSpeedMul: Heavy: gravity multiplier. Applied to the GRAVITY attribute rather than by shoving the player downward, so acceleration, terminal velocity and fall distance all stay vanilla's — just heavier. NOTE the attribute is hard-capped at 1.0 by the game.
witchmod.configuration.heavyFallDamageMu: Heavy: fall damage multiplier, on top of the extra distance the faster fall racks up.
witchmod.configuration.heavyCraterMinFal: Heavy: how far you must fall, in blocks, before you land hard enough to crater.
witchmod.configuration.heavyCraterCapFal: Heavy: the fall distance at which the crater stops growing — THE CAP. Beyond this a longer drop is no more destructive, so a void-height fall can't level a base.
witchmod.configuration.heavyCraterPowerM: Heavy: explosion power at exactly the minimum fall distance. (TNT is 4.0.)
Heavy: explosion power once the fall reaches the cap.
witchmod.configuration.heavyCraterSelfDa: Heavy: percent of its own crater blast the faller takes. They're at dead centre AND have just eaten amplified fall damage, so full blast damage would execute them every single time.
witchmod.configuration.heavyJumpCompensa: Heavy: multiplier on JUMP_STRENGTH, purely so a single block stays climbable. Jump apex is roughly v^2/(2*gravity), so heavier gravity alone drops a normal 1.25-block jump to about 0.6 — under the one block you need, which makes the curse a nuisance rather than a joke. 1.35 puts the apex just over a block: you can still get up a step, but nothing about it feels light. Raise if you change heavyFallSpeedMultiplier.
witchmod.configuration.heavyCraterCooldo: Heavy: minimum ticks between craters. Stops the blast chaining — a crater blows the ground out from under you, so you fall again, crater again, and keep digging yourself downward. 60 = 3s.
witchmod.configuration.heavyWaterPull.to: Heavy: extra downward pull per tick while in water or lava — you sink like an anchor. Needed as its own value because vanilla divides gravity by 16 in fluid, so the GRAVITY attribute alone just gives a slightly brisker version of the same gentle bob. Applied client-side, since player movement is client-authoritative. For reference, a full swim-up tops out around 0.048/tick, so anything at or above that makes surfacing impossible.
witchmod.configuration.heavyCraterKnockb: Heavy: knockback multiplier for the crater blast — the shockwave that throws everything standing nearby.
witchmod.configuration.gassyIntervalMinT: Gassy: shortest gap between spontaneous farts. 400 = 20s.
witchmod.configuration.gassyIntervalMaxT: Gassy: longest gap between spontaneous farts. 1200 = 60s.
witchmod.configuration.gassyBigFartChanc: Gassy: percent chance a spontaneous fart is a BIG one (different sound, more velocity).
witchmod.configuration.gassyBigFartMulti: Gassy: velocity multiplier for a big fart.
witchmod.configuration.gassyRandomDirect: Gassy: percent chance a fart ignores nearby hazards entirely and fires off in a random direction. This is what stops the curse being a guaranteed lava delivery service — the hazard bias must never be a certainty.
witchmod.configuration.gassyHazardScanRa: Gassy: how far to look for something worth being launched into, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.gassyLedgeDropMin: Gassy: how many clear blocks below a spot make it count as a ledge worth aiming at.
witchmod.configuration.gassyStraightUpCh: Gassy: percent chance a fart is mostly straight UP rather than off in a direction.
Gassy: smallest upward kick added to a directional fart, so you get some air either way. This is a RATIO against the horizontal, not an absolute speed — the launch vector is normalised before the velocity is applied, so raising these tilts farts upward without making them stronger.
Gassy: largest upward kick added to a directional fart. See gassyVerticalMin — a ratio.
witchmod.configuration.gassyOnDamageChan: Gassy: percent chance that taking a hit frightens one out of you.
witchmod.configuration.gassyOnExplosionC: Gassy: percent chance a nearby explosion or firework sets one off. Much likelier than a plain hit — the whole joke is the sympathetic detonation.
witchmod.configuration.gassyEventBigFart: Gassy Event Big Fart Chance Percent
Gassy: percent chance an event-triggered fart is a BIG one. Deliberately far higher than the spontaneous rate.
witchmod.configuration.gassyEventVelocit: Gassy: extra velocity multiplier on event-triggered farts, on top of any big-fart bonus.
witchmod.configuration.gassyEventCooldow: Gassy: minimum ticks between event-triggered farts, so one firework show doesn't launch you forty times.
witchmod.configuration.gassyExplosionHea: Gassy: how close an explosion or firework must be to set one off, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsMaxConcu: Delusions: how many fake players may be visible at once. Low on purpose — a crowd of them reads as a glitch, one lurking at the treeline reads as a person.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsSpawnInt: Delusions: shortest gap between one appearing. 1200 = 60s.
Delusions: longest gap between one appearing. 3600 = 3min.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsSpawnRan: Delusions: closest one will appear, in blocks. Never right on top of you.
Delusions: furthest one will appear, in blocks.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsLifetime: Delusions: longest one sticks around before quietly vanishing. 1200 = 60s.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsDespawnD: Delusions: one further away than this is dropped (you wandered off, or it did).
witchmod.configuration.delusionsStateSwa: Delusions: average ticks a behaviour lasts before it picks another. Each state rolls its own length around this, so they don't all switch on the same beat.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsRealisat: Delusions: how long you must have one in view (in your view cone AND in line of sight) before it can notice you back. 60 = 3s of staring.
Delusions: percent chance per second, once you've watched one long enough, that it turns around and stares back.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsChargeCh: Delusions: percent chance a realisation ends with it SPRINTING AT YOU rather than just vanishing where it stands.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsHitReach: Delusions: how far your swing reaches one, in blocks. They are deliberately NOT pickable by vanilla's crosshair (that would send the server an attack packet for an entity it has never heard of), so the swing is ray-traced against them separately.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsViewCone: Delusions: how centred in your view one must be to count as 'seen'. 0.75 is roughly a 41-degree cone off your crosshair; lower widens it.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsObserveD: Delusions: how close one gets before it stops and just watches you, in blocks. Close enough to be uncomfortable, far enough that it isn't touching you.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsMirrorSe: Delusions: whether YOUR OWN skin and name can be used for a fake player. When you are the only player online it is used regardless — there is nobody else to be.
witchmod.configuration.delusionsMisident: Delusions: how many REAL players can be misidentified at once — shown to the victim wearing the wrong player's skin + nametag. 0 disables the misidentification entirely.
Delusions: minimum ticks between a new real-player misidentification starting. 400 = 20s.
Delusions: maximum ticks between a new real-player misidentification starting. 1600 = 80s.
Delusions: minimum ticks a misidentification lasts before the real player looks like themselves again. 200 = 10s.
Delusions: maximum ticks a misidentification lasts. 600 = 30s.
witchmod.configuration.effectCostOverrid: Per-effect essence cost overrides, format "witchmod:effect_id=cost". Any effect not listed here keeps its code-defined default cost.
witchmod.configuration.lowGravityGravity: Low Gravity: multiplier on the GRAVITY attribute — the whole floaty feel (slower fall + higher float). <1 = lighter.
witchmod.configuration.lowGravityJumpMul: Low Gravity: multiplier on JUMP_STRENGTH — how much higher your jumps launch.
witchmod.configuration.lowGravityFallDam: Low Gravity: multiplier on fall damage taken (soft landings).
witchmod.configuration.berserkerReductio: Berserker: attack-cooldown reduction gained per consecutive landed hit, as a fraction (0.07 = 7%).
witchmod.configuration.berserkerMaxReduc: Berserker: maximum total attack-cooldown reduction (0.80 = 80% shorter cooldown, i.e. ~5x faster).
witchmod.configuration.berserkerMaxStack: Berserker: the total consecutive-hit stacks you can build (the reduction still caps at berserkerMaxReduction).
witchmod.configuration.berserkerResetSec: Berserker: seconds without landing a hit before the whole stack resets (also resets instantly on a miss).
witchmod.configuration.berserkerGladiato: Berserker+Gladiator synergy: berserker stacks granted per successful parry.
witchmod.configuration.enchanterXpReduct: Enchanter: fraction (0..1) of the XP-level cost of enchanting-table use that is refunded. 0.8 = 80% cheaper (small costs become free).
witchmod.configuration.enchanterLevelBon: Enchanter: how many extra enchant levels each of the table's three options is bumped by (better enchants by default).
witchmod.configuration.pacifierRadius.to: Pacifier: radius (blocks) of the anti-grief aura for entities — primed TNT, creepers, fireballs.
witchmod.configuration.pacifierBlockRadi: Pacifier: radius (blocks) within which spreading fire is snuffed out.
witchmod.configuration.pacifierCheckInte: Pacifier: how often (ticks) the aura sweeps. Lower = snappier, more work.
witchmod.configuration.oceansSwimBoost.t: Ocean's Blessing: modest baseline forward velocity added per tick while swimming (a small nudge on its own — the real speed comes from dolphins).
witchmod.configuration.oceansDolphinMult: Ocean's Blessing: multiplier on the swim boost while you have Dolphin's Grace (from an attracted dolphin) — this is where the big speed lives.
witchmod.configuration.oceansMaxSpeed.to: Ocean's Blessing: cap on horizontal swim speed (blocks/tick) the boost will drive you to.
witchmod.configuration.oceansPacifyRadiu: Ocean's Blessing: radius (blocks) within which aggressive mobs are pacified toward you while you're in water.
witchmod.configuration.oceansDolphinAttr: Ocean's Blessing: wide radius (blocks) from which dolphins are drawn to you and made to follow.
witchmod.configuration.oceansDolphinGrac: Ocean's Blessing: how close a dolphin must be (blocks) to grant you Dolphin's Grace (and thus the big speed).
witchmod.configuration.oceansDolphinNavS: Ocean's Blessing: navigation speed multiplier used when steering attracted dolphins toward you.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorWindowTi: Gladiator: length of the parry window (ticks) after right-clicking a sword/axe. 4 = 0.2s — tight, demands precision.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorFrontDot: Gladiator: how 'in front' the attacker must be to parry (dot of look vs direction-to-attacker; higher = narrower frontal arc).
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorRiposteD: Gladiator: NORMAL riposte damage as a multiple of your weapon's swing damage.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorPerfectD: Gladiator: PERFECT-parry riposte damage multiple (a tight, early parry).
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorPerfectT: Gladiator: how tight the PERFECT window is — a parry landing within this many ticks of the danger counts as perfect. 2 = 0.1s.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorPerfectS: Gladiator: how long (ticks) a PERFECT parry stuns the foe (heavy Slowness+Weakness) so the riposte knockback throws them. 10 = 0.5s.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorLeewayTi: Gladiator: reactive leeway — you can still parry for this many ticks AFTER a hit lands (press it just late). ~4 = 0.18s.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorWhiffLoc: Gladiator: while parrying you can't switch/swing/use your hand; a WHIFF extends that lock by this many ticks (2 = 0.1s) as extra risk.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorSwordCoo: Gladiator: weapon swing cooldown imposed by a SUCCESSFUL parry (riposte/reflect) — a sword's timing. 13 ~ 0.65s (sword attack speed 1.6).
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorAxeCoold: Gladiator: weapon swing cooldown imposed by a WHIFF — an axe's timing (slower). 22 ~ 1.1s (axe attack speed ~0.9).
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorRiposteK: Gladiator: extra knockback strength dealt by the riposte (perfect parries throw a little harder). Kept modest so foes don't fly.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorShakeStr: Gladiator: base camera-shake strength on a parry (perfect shakes harder, whiff softer — scaled from this).
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorShakeTic: Gladiator: how long (ticks) the parry camera shake decays over.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorRiposteD: Gladiator: short delay (ticks) between a successful parry and the riposte hit landing.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorCooldown: Gladiator: parry cooldown after a SUCCESSFUL parry (seconds).
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorWhiffCoo: Gladiator: parry cooldown after a WHIFFED parry (seconds) — the success cooldown plus a 0.25s mistiming penalty.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorReflectS: Gladiator: launch speed of a reflected projectile, sent where you're LOOKING. A touch higher than incoming, but still fairly low.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorProjecti: Gladiator: extra ticks of slack on EACH side of the window for PROJECTILE parries (they're harder to time than melee, so more forgiving). 3 = ~0.15s.
witchmod.configuration.gladiatorReflectA: Gladiator: half-angle (degrees) of the cone around your look within which a reflected projectile will assist-aim at an entity.
Gladiator: how strongly a reflect leans toward an in-cone entity (0 = pure look direction, 1 = straight at the entity).
Gladiator: how far (blocks) the reflect assist-aim looks for an entity in the cone.
witchmod.configuration.tankBonusHealth.t: Tank: bonus max health added via a MAX_HEALTH attribute (no status-effect UI at all). 20 = a whole extra health bar.
witchmod.configuration.tankRegenMultipli: Tank: multiplier on natural-regeneration healing (small heals) — significantly slower regen. 0.35 = 35% of normal.
Spider: upward climb speed against a wall (blocks/tick). Vanilla spiders climb at ~0.2; higher is faster.
Spider: upward launch when you jump off a wall.
witchmod.configuration.spiderWallJumpAwa: Spider: horizontal 'kick off' away from the wall when wall-jumping.
witchmod.configuration.spiderWallJumpCoo: Spider: minimum ticks between wall jumps (so one jump press = one kick).
Ninja: extra movement speed as a fraction (0.25 = +25%), applied as a MOVEMENT_SPEED multiplier.
Ninja: extra attack speed as a fraction (0.8 = +80% -> much faster swing recovery/animation).
witchmod.configuration.ninjaDoubleJumpPo: Ninja: upward velocity of the mid-air second jump (a bit stronger than a normal jump).
witchmod.configuration.ninjaSwingPitch.t: Ninja: pitch (speed) of the parry-whiff woosh played on each weapon swing. 1.7 = quick and sharp.
witchmod.configuration.ninjaKnockbackMul: Ninja: knockback multiplier on YOUR melee hits — 0.34 = 66% less, so victims barely stagger and you stay on them. Disregarded (no reduction) if you also carry a knockback-boosting effect like Heavy Hitter or Main Character.
witchmod.configuration.backstabDamageMul: Backstabbing: melee damage multiplier when you hit a target from behind. Multiplies the final damage, so it STACKS with crits/enchants.
witchmod.configuration.backstabKnockback: Backstabbing: knockback multiplier on a backstab (less knockback so you stay on them).
witchmod.configuration.backstabPlayerDot: Backstabbing vs PLAYERS: attacker counts as 'behind' when the dot of the victim's look and the direction-to-attacker is at/below this. Lower = stricter (must be well behind).
witchmod.configuration.backstabMobDot.to: Backstabbing vs MOBS: same threshold but MORE GENEROUS (mob AI faces you, so a wider rear arc counts). Higher = easier.
witchmod.configuration.backstabSoundPitc: Backstabbing: pitch of the riposte 'impact' sound played on a successful backstab.
witchmod.configuration.propHuntStillTick: Prop Hunt: how long (ticks) you must crouch and stand still before you disguise as the block below you. 20 = 1s.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorCheckInt: Solicitor: how often (ticks) the curse re-checks/steers the trader.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorMoveSpee: Solicitor: the trader's base MOVEMENT_SPEED attribute — low so it ambles rather than blitzing about (vanilla trader is ~0.5).
witchmod.configuration.solicitorFollowSp: Solicitor: navigation speed multiplier while walking toward you.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorFollowDi: Solicitor: it only walks toward you when further than this (blocks); closer than it, it STOPS so you can actually trade with it.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorTeleport: Solicitor: if the trader falls further than this (blocks) behind you, it teleports closer (it never gives up).
witchmod.configuration.solicitorChatMinT: Solicitor: shortest gap (ticks) between the trader's chat pitches.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorChatMaxT: Solicitor: longest gap (ticks) between the trader's chat pitches.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorChatRadi: Solicitor: how far (blocks) from the trader its chat pitches are heard.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorHideMinS: Solicitor: minimum time (seconds) the trader stays gone after you actually complete a trade with it.
witchmod.configuration.solicitorHideMaxS: Solicitor: maximum time (seconds) gone after a trade — the roll is biased toward the LONGER end.
witchmod.configuration.snailBaseSpeedBlo: Snail Base Speed Blocks Per Second
The Snail: THE fundamental balancing constant — base chase speed in BLOCKS PER SECOND (its speed when right on top of you).
witchmod.configuration.snailDistanceScal: The Snail: how much its speed grows per block of distance (0.08 = +8% base speed per block away) — slow when close, much faster when far.
witchmod.configuration.snailMaxSpeedBloc: Snail Max Speed Blocks Per Second
The Snail: hard cap on its chase speed (blocks/second), however far away you get.
witchmod.configuration.snailTouchDistanc: The Snail: how close (blocks) it must get to touch you and detonate.
witchmod.configuration.snailSpawnDistanc: The Snail: how far away (blocks) it starts, and re-appears after catching you.
witchmod.configuration.snailMaterialiseR: The Snail: within this distance (blocks) the real entity is spawned/shown; beyond it only the virtual position is tracked (nothing loaded).
witchmod.configuration.snailMusicDistanc: The Snail: max distance (blocks) the music can be heard; it fades in from here and stops beyond it.
witchmod.configuration.snailMusicFullDis: The Snail: within this distance (blocks) the music is at full volume; between it and the max distance it fades.
The Snail: volume of the looping music.
witchmod.configuration.snailExplodePower: The Snail: explosion power when it reaches you (also dealt lethal directly, so it's an instant kill barring a totem/Last Stand).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerAngerMax.t: The Dweller: the anger ceiling; the closer to it, the closer the chase.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerBaseAngerP: The Dweller: anger it gains every second no matter what — the slow, inevitable escalation. VERY low: at max (100) with the dark/alone accelerants a dread session should take ~13-18 min to peak. The big driver is being ALONE + in the DARK.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerViewConeDo: The Dweller: how centred in your view it must be to count as 'looked at' (dot product; higher = you must look more directly at it).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTier1Thres: The Dweller: anger at which it moves from Far observation to Close observation.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTier2Thres: The Dweller: anger at which it moves from Close observation to Inspection (it starts coming close).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTier3Thres: The Dweller: anger at which it enters the Chase tier (fake chases, then the real one).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerFarDistanc: The Dweller: distance (blocks) it watches from during Far observation.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerInspectDis: The Dweller: distance (blocks) it stands at during Inspection — right in your space.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTouchDista: The Dweller: how close (blocks) it must get during the chase to catch and kill you.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerPassiveCol: The Dweller: during a chase, colliding with ANY passive entity (an animal, villager, golem) instantly triggers the gory finale too — nowhere is safe once it's hunting you.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseStrid: The Dweller: blocks the dweller must walk between footstep sounds during a chase (its stride length). Larger = fewer, more spaced-out steps. Tuned to match the movement speed.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerShakeTicks: The Dweller: how long (ticks) the on-hit camera shake lasts (bang-behind / lunge / the finale).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerShakeStren: The Dweller: peak camera-shake strength (degrees of random jolt) for the on-hit shake.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerWatchVanis: The Dweller: any passive WATCH vanishes the moment you get within this many blocks of it (you can never close on a watch — it blinks away).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseMinCo: The Dweller: the SHORTEST chase cooldown (ticks) — reached at MAX dread. The cooldown is the window where the game won't roll a new chase; at max dread it's tiny, so hunts come back almost instantly. Default 5s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerMaxDreadLo: The Dweller: at MAX dread, how long (ticks) you must hold eye contact with it before it goes aggressive and the hunt begins. Low = looking at it is near-instant death sentence.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseStuck: The Dweller: how long (ticks) the chase can fail to make progress (truly walled in, unable to path/climb/break through) before it subtly teleports closer as a LAST-RESORT fallback. Higher = the good AI is relied on more and teleports are rarer.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseRampT: The Dweller: how long (ticks) a chase takes to ramp from its slow starting speed up to full pace. The hunt starts a touch slow and builds momentum.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerBridgeChas: The Dweller: chance (0-1) that a watch/sizeup/lunge BRIDGES straight into a chase at the chase floor (low dread). The hunt can erupt from where the creature stands rather than always resetting.
The Dweller: chance (0-1) that a watch/sizeup/lunge bridges into a chase at MAX dread. Higher dread = the creature commits to the hunt from its current spot far more readily.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerSizeupStar: The Dweller: during a SIZEUP (it stands right in front of you, passive), how long (ticks) you can stare back before its aggression ramps and it lunges/hunts.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerLungeSpeed: The Dweller: the phantom-CHARGE speed (blocks/tick) of a lunge — it visibly rushes you at this pace, and the jumpscare fires the instant it arrives. Lower = a slower, more followable charge (not a teleport).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerLungeMaxTi: The Dweller: safety cap (ticks) on a lunge charge — it normally ends the instant it reaches you, but times out after this if something blocks the arrival.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseLunge: The Dweller: minimum dread fraction (0-1) for the mid-chase ravager LUNGE to be possible. Only higher dread earns the launch-at-you attacks.
The Dweller: max distance (blocks) at which a mid-chase lunge can start.
The Dweller: distancegain lunge speed (blocks/second) — the straight launch at you used generally / as a close finisher. Fast but locked, so a sidestep dodges it.
The Dweller: CLIMB lunge speed (blocks/second) — the upward-arcing launch that counters height-camping. Slightly slower so the vertical arc reads.
The Dweller: how long (ticks) a mid-chase lunge stays in its locked flight before it settles back to the walking chase if it missed.
The Dweller: cooldown (ticks) between mid-chase lunges, so it doesn't chain launches back-to-back.
The Dweller: how many blocks ABOVE the chaser you must be for a lunge to use the upward CLIMB variant (counter height-camping) instead of the straight distancegain launch.
The Dweller: the UPWARD velocity (blocks/tick) of a CLIMB leap — how high it jumps to reach a player camping on height. ~0.42 clears 1 block; 0.85 clears ~4.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseMoveS: The Dweller: the chaser's MOVEMENT_SPEED attribute during a hunt. For a MOB this scale runs ~0.25 = a walk, so ~0.34 is a hard relentless sprint clearly faster than a fleeing player. The navigation multiplier below scales this further.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseSprin: The Dweller: the base navigation SPEED MULTIPLIER on the chase MOVEMENT_SPEED (1.0 = sprint pace). A small in-hunt ramp (0.85→1.0) and dread bonus (+18% at max) ride on top.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseWater: The Dweller: swim speed (blocks/tick) it's pushed toward you while IN WATER during a chase, so it powers across water fast instead of getting stuck. 0.5 ~ 10 b/s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseStart: The Dweller: how far behind you a FRESH chase places the creature by default (further away now, so a hunt has run-up).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerCloseChase: The Dweller: the CLOSECHASE start distance — the old, much closer default. A fresh chase uses this instead of the far start on a dread-scaling chance.
The Dweller: chance (0-1) at LOW dread that a fresh chase is a CLOSECHASE (starts at the close distance rather than far).
The Dweller: chance (0-1) at MAX dread that a fresh chase is a CLOSECHASE. Higher dread = far more likely to start right on top of you.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseMinSt: The Dweller: SAFETY floor — if a chase would begin closer than this (e.g. a sizeup/close watch bridging within a few blocks), the creature is pulled BACK to a safe start distance so it can't be an instant, uncounterable touch-kill.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEventInter: The Dweller: minimum gap (ticks) between staged events (repositions, watches, breaks). Scaled shorter at higher tiers.
The Dweller: maximum gap (ticks) between staged events. Scaled shorter at higher tiers.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerBedBreakCh: The Dweller: chance a Sleep-watch event smashes the bed you're in (kicking you out of it).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerDoorBreakC: The Dweller: chance an event breaks a nearby door/trapdoor/glass to unnerve you (from tier 2).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerExplodeEnt: The Dweller: explosion power when it detonates a nearby animal/villager as a warning (0 = kill it silently).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerDormantMin: The Dweller: minimum absence (ticks) between appearances at tier 0. Early FAR glimpses are meant to be fairly frequent (just distant); the absence shrinks smoothly as dread climbs.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerDormantMax: The Dweller: maximum absence (ticks) between appearances at tier 0. Shrinks smoothly as dread climbs.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerManifestMi: The Dweller: minimum time (ticks) a single appearance lasts before it melts away (at tier 0 — brief glimpses). Longer at higher tiers.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerManifestMa: The Dweller: maximum time (ticks) a single appearance lasts. Longer at higher tiers.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerBoredomBoo: The Dweller (BOREDOM): extra dread per second at low tiers (0-1) when no encounter has happened for a while — stops the early game stalling because nothing is pushing the tiers up.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerBoredomDel: The Dweller (BOREDOM): how long (ticks) with no encounter before the boredom boost kicks in. Default 4s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTier0Stuck: The Dweller (BOREDOM): ticks stuck at TIER 0 before an ADDITIONAL dread boost is added. Default 4.5min.
Dweller Tier0 Stuck Boost Per Second
The Dweller (BOREDOM): extra dread per second once you've been stuck at tier 0 past dwellerTier0StuckTicks.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerInteractDr: The Dweller: bonus dread added each time you INTERACT with one of its effects instead of ignoring it — swinging at the stalker, or getting too close to a watch/mimic. The counterplay is to ignore, so engaging costs you.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTellMinTic: The Dweller: minimum length (ticks) of the TELL beat — the anticipation window before an appearance (heartbeat starts + quickens, a sign lands). Shrinks as dread climbs. Default ~3s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerTellMaxTic: The Dweller: maximum length (ticks) of the TELL anticipation beat. Default ~6s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerReleaseMin: The Dweller: minimum length (ticks) of the RELEASE beat — the pointed quiet AFTER a scare, before the next lull. The exhale. Default ~4s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerReleaseMax: The Dweller: maximum length (ticks) of the RELEASE exhale beat. Default ~8s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerStareVanis: The Dweller: staring straight at ANY watch for this long (ticks) makes it vanish — the double-take. Default 3s (60t). At high dread the vanish is instead a lunge/chase bridge, but the trigger time is the same.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerWatchAnger: The Dweller: extra anger per second while you are actively looking at it — it hates being seen, so watching it hastens the end.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerAmbientMin: The Dweller: minimum gap (ticks) between the ambient dread cues (footsteps, breaths, a knock) it makes even while absent.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerAmbientMax: The Dweller: maximum gap (ticks) between ambient dread cues.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEyesMin.to: The Dweller (Watchers event): minimum number of glowing-eye pairs that appear in the dark.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEyesMax.to: The Dweller (Watchers event): maximum number of glowing-eye pairs.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEyesDistan: The Dweller (Watchers event): how far out (blocks) the eyes hang, ringed around you in the dark.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEyesMinTic: The Dweller (Watchers event): minimum time (ticks) the eyes watch before fading.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEyesMaxTic: The Dweller (Watchers event): maximum time (ticks) the eyes watch before fading.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerKnockBlock: The Dweller (Knock event): how many nearby doors/glass get knocked on (then shattered).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerKnockShatt: The Dweller (Knock event): minimum delay (ticks) after the knock before every doomed block shatters at once (1s default).
The Dweller (Knock event): maximum delay (ticks) after the knock before the shatter (6s default) — the long, silent pause is the point.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerHallucinat: The Dweller: minimum gap (ticks) between AUDITORY hallucinations — fake footsteps, mining, chests, other-player sounds. Deliberately LONG so they stay rare and impactful; tier 0 is ~2.2x rarer still.
The Dweller: maximum gap (ticks) between auditory hallucinations.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerDarkDreadP: The Dweller: EXTRA dread per second while standing in DARKNESS (light <= dwellerDarkLightLevel). The dark is where it thrives.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerIsolationD: The Dweller: EXTRA dread per second while you are ALONE (no other player within dwellerCompanyRadius). The dominant driver — being alone with it is where the horror lives, so this is large.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerNightDread: The Dweller: EXTRA dread per second at NIGHT.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerEnclosedDr: The Dweller: EXTRA dread per second while ENCLOSED (no sky above you) — trapped underground with it.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerLightCalmP: The Dweller (COUNTERPLAY): dread CALMED per second while standing in bright light (light >= dwellerLightLevel), scaled by how bright.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerCompanyCal: The Dweller (COUNTERPLAY): dread CALMED per second per nearby player (capped at 3) — safety in numbers.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerDaylightCa: The Dweller (COUNTERPLAY): dread CALMED per second in open DAYLIGHT (day + sky access) — it hates the sun.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerIgnoreCalm: The Dweller (COUNTERPLAY): dread CALMED per second while it is manifest and you are NOT looking at it — the real reward for ignoring it. Dread can now fall (never below 0), but the accelerants keep it climbing overall if you can't stay calm.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerForeplayMi: The Dweller (FOREPLAY): minimum length (ticks) of the opening phase — no fog/desaturation, music plays, only the odd VERY distant watch. Default 40s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerForeplayMa: The Dweller (FOREPLAY): maximum length (ticks) of the opening phase. Default 3min.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerForeplayWa: Dweller Foreplay Watch Gap Min Ticks
The Dweller (FOREPLAY): minimum gap (ticks) between the rare distant watches during the opening phase.
Dweller Foreplay Watch Gap Max Ticks
The Dweller (FOREPLAY): maximum gap (ticks) between the rare distant watches during the opening phase.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseMinTi: The Dweller: minimum length (ticks) of a chase before it breaks off (if it can't catch you). Default 20s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerCompanyRad: The Dweller: radius (blocks) within which other players count as company (calming you and making it shy).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerLightLevel: The Dweller: light level at/above which you count as 'in the light' (calming, repels it).
The Dweller: light level at/below which you count as 'in the dark' (dread rises, it grows bold).
witchmod.configuration.dwellerLightLurkD: The Dweller (COUNTERPLAY): while you're in bright light, it will not creep closer than this (blocks) — it lurks at the edge of the light.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseMaxTi: The Dweller: maximum length (ticks) of a chase — each hunt rolls a duration in [chaseMinTicks, chaseMaxTicks] and breaks off at that if it can't catch you. Default 35s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseCoold: The Dweller: the LONGEST chase cooldown (ticks) — used at the moment dread first enters the chase range. Scales DOWN toward dwellerChaseMinCooldownTicks as dread climbs to max. Default 20s.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerMimicBurst: The Dweller (Mimic event): how long (ticks) it refreshes the Delusions fake-player system for a fresh wave of impostors.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerFinaleExpl: The Dweller (finale): explosion power at the death spot so the catch goes off like the explosion event (gory burst + a real blast that hurts nearby others). 0 = gore only. NO terrain damage.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerChaseTelep: The Dweller: how far (blocks) it blinks away to when it teleports mid-hunt.
witchmod.configuration.dwellerHeartbeatM: The Dweller: FASTEST gap (ticks) between the oppressive heartbeat you hear — reached at max dread / when it's right on top of you.
The Dweller: SLOWEST gap (ticks) between heartbeats — the languid pulse of low dread.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockEventMinTi: Bedrock Moment: minimum gap (ticks) between ACTIVE bug events. It's an overloaded curse, so they come thick and fast.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockEventMaxTi: Bedrock Moment: maximum gap (ticks) between active bug events.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockTier1Weigh: Bedrock Moment: pool weight of a TIER 1 (very common) active event.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockTier2Weigh: Bedrock Moment: pool weight of a TIER 2 (medium rarity) active event.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockTier3Weigh: Bedrock Moment: pool weight of a TIER 3 (rare) active event.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockGhostItemT: Bedrock Moment (Ghost Item): how long (ticks) your held item renders as a random other item.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockInputLagTi: Bedrock Moment (Input Lag): how long (ticks) the input-lag window lasts.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockInputLagDe: Bedrock Moment (Input Lag): how many ticks late your movement input is applied.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockTextureFli: Bedrock Moment (Texture Flicker): how long (ticks) the missing-texture flicker window lasts.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockSprintRese: Bedrock Moment (Sprint Reset): how long (ticks) sprint keeps cutting out.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockGhostPhase: Bedrock Moment (Ghost Block Phase): min length (ticks) of the ghost-block spell (blocks placed/broken revert).
Bedrock Moment (Ghost Block Phase): max length (ticks) of the ghost-block spell (default 4–16s).
witchmod.configuration.bedrockFoodRegCha: Bedrock Moment (Food Reg): % chance an eaten food provides NO hunger (desync).
witchmod.configuration.bedrockHitRegChan: Bedrock Moment (Hit Reg): % chance a melee hit is invalidated (whiffs to the empty-swing sound).
witchmod.configuration.bedrockLanguageTi: Bedrock Moment (Language Error): how long (ticks) the language stays swapped to pirate/welsh.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockSpeedBlitz: Bedrock Moment (Speed Blitz): how long (ticks) you're frozen while your movement is stored.
Bedrock Moment (Fake BSOD): how long (ticks) the blue screen is shown.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockAirSwimCha: Bedrock Moment (Air Swimming): per-tick chance, WHILE swimming, that you keep swimming after leaving water.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockAirSwimMin: Bedrock Moment (Air Swimming): minimum ticks the air-swim lasts before it's force-cancelled.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockPauseMobMi: Bedrock Moment (Pause): min ticks nearby entities are paused (AI off + frozen).
witchmod.configuration.bedrockPauseCatch: Bedrock Moment (Pause): after unpausing, entities tick THIS many times per tick (higher than tickspeed) to 'catch up'.
Bedrock Moment (Pause): min ticks of the post-unpause catch-up burst.
Bedrock Moment (Pause): max ticks of the catch-up burst (default 1–4s).
witchmod.configuration.bedrockFloatTicks: Bedrock Moment (Float): how long (ticks) affected entities lose gravity.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockFloatChanc: Bedrock Moment (Float): per-entity chance each nearby entity loses gravity.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockSleepCance: Bedrock Moment (Sleep Cancel): per-tick chance, while sleeping, to be booted out of the bed.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockCooldownsM: Bedrock Moment (Cooldowns — beneficial): min duration (ticks) of the quartered swing cooldown. Default 8s.
Bedrock Moment (Cooldowns — beneficial): max duration (ticks). Default 28s.
witchmod.configuration.bedrockCooldownsA: Bedrock Moment (Cooldowns — beneficial): ATTACK_SPEED multiplier during the window. 4.0 = quartered cooldown (4x swings), Bedrock-style.
